items.title: What is the maximum $k$ for a $k$-gon inducible with an $n$-line arrangement?
items.body:
Consider a $k$-gon with sides $S_1,S_2,S_3,\dots,S_k$. Denote the underlying line of a side $S_i$ by $L_i$. Note that for two sides to be adjacent and share a vertex, it must be that their underlying lines intersect at that vertex. Since two lines intersect only at one point, it means that the loop $(L_1L_2L_3\dots L_k)$ must satisfy the following:

  1. Adjacent $L_i$'s (including $L_kL_1$) must not be equal.
  2. Each adjacent pair must be distinct.

Thus, construct a graph with $L_i$ as vertices. Note that there are $n$ vertices since $L_i$ are not distinct. Connect the vertices if they are ever adjacent in the loop. Since each adjacent pair is distinct, each edge is traversed exactly once. And since it is a loop, the graph is an Eulerian cycle. Consulting $A050187$ from the OEIS, we have an upper bound of $k \le n\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor$.

I suspect that the bound is exact for all $n$, i.e. $k = n\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor$. However, I cannot construct an example satisfying the equality for $n\ge7$.

If polygons with non-zero genuses are allowed, then I cannot construct an example for $n\ge11$, though such polygons would break the proof above. Any help is appreciated.

For your reference, here are my examples for $n<11$:

  • $n=3$: Trivial.
  • $n=4$: Trivial.
  • $n=5$: Consider a five-pointed star.
  • $n=6$: Consider the Star of David.
  • $n=7$: Consider the following construction based on $\{7/3\}$:
  • $n=8$: Solved by DSM; a 24-gon with 8 lines is possible. (genus 0 solution)
  • $n=9,10$: A similar construction to $n=7$ can be done.

However, for $n=11$, the same construction does not yield one connected polygon, so the question remains unsolved. I wonder if it is possible to somehow prove that only a genus 1 polygon can satisfy $n=7$.

A natural follow-up question to ask would be whether a genus 0 construction is always possible, but that probably deserves its own thread.
